_comment: This is rulesync 15.1.0's CANONICAL schema, not Claude Code's native one. The event key is camelCase `preToolUse` (rulesync maps it to `PreToolUse` on generate), and each definition is FLAT -- matcher/type/command as siblings -- because rulesync builds the nested {matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]} shape itself. Feed it Claude Code's native PascalCase/nested shape and rulesync skips the event AND silently drops the command: that is how this file shipped inert once already. The top-level `hooks` record is required by rulesync's Zod schema even though only the claudecode override carries content. WHAT OMITTING IT DOES, RE-MEASURED ON THE PINNED VERSION: generate prints a Zod error, exits 0, and still writes 11 of its 12 outputs -- CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/ -- under the ordinary `All done!` summary, with ONLY .claude/settings.json missing. Under the version pinned before this one the same omission wrote nothing at all and printed `All files are up to date`. So this failure mode CHANGED SHAPE across a bump, and inverted in the dangerous direction: from an empty tree nobody could miss, to a near-complete one whose single absent file is the one carrying the guard. Re-measure it on the next bump rather than trusting this sentence -- that is the whole reason it is spelled out. Two gates catch it regardless of the wording here: scripts/guard_rulesync_drift.py compares the emitted counts against a pinned map and sees 1 hook expected against 0, and scripts/guard_emitted_outputs.py reads the emitted .claude/settings.json STRUCTURALLY -- it requires a command that RUNS the guard to sit at hooks.PreToolUse[*].hooks[*] with type command, the one path Claude Code executes -- which fails closed when the file is absent. Not a grep: a grep proves only that the string is somewhere in the document, and a command re-nested under another event, carried on a non-command hook, or merely echoed satisfies it while running nothing. AGAINST A HUMAN EDIT, tests/test_hooks_wiring.py pins this shape and this comment is only a courtesy. AGAINST A RULESYNC VERSION BUMP, this comment is the FIRST defence and no longer the only one: the offline suite asserts THIS file, so a rulesync that renamed `preToolUse` or re-nested the definitions would leave it green -- but the emitted-output guard reads the generated ARTIFACT, so it catches the dropped command whatever the input schema was renamed to. Re-verify the emitted .claude/settings.json by hand when changing the pinned version in package.json.
